heading: INT. MARCHETTI PAWN AND LOAN, BACK ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MARCHETTI PAWN AND LOAN, BACK ROOM - NIGHT
A single green-shaded lamp.
Shelves of wristwatches, trumpets, wedding bands in cigar boxes.
The shop's front shutters are down, and rain taps the steel.
LOU MARCHETTI, sixties, in suspenders and a rumpled shirt, sits at a rolltop desk counting bills into a drawer.
DETECTIVE IRENE KOWALCZYK, forties, trench coat belted tight, stands by a shelf of cameras.
She turns one over in her hands as if it interests her.
ARTIE, nineteen, the stock boy, stands in the doorway holding a broom.
He has not swept anything.
He glances at the desk.
She notices him glance.
Quiet night, Mr. Marchetti.
units.name: KOWALCZYK

units.text: They're all quiet. I run a quiet place.
units.name: LOU

units.text: She sets down the camera and picks up a pocket watch.
She holds it to her ear, then to the light.
Funny. This one's engraved. "To Walter, from Dora, 1951." You buy this last week?
units.name: KOWALCZYK

units.text: I buy a lot of things.
units.name: LOU

units.text: Walter Pinski. He was found in the river on Tuesday.
units.name: KOWALCZYK

units.text: Lou counts another bill.
He puts it in the drawer, closes the drawer, and rests both hands on top of it.
Artie lets the broom slide until the handle taps the floor.
Lou looks at him.
Artie picks it up again, too fast.
Artie. Go home.
units.name: LOU

units.text: It's raining, Mr. Marchetti.
units.name: ARTIE

units.text: Go home anyway.
units.name: LOU

units.text: He leaves.
The bell over the front door rings once, thin and far away.
She sets the watch gently on the desk in front of Lou and sits down opposite him, unbuttoning her coat.
Take your time.
units.name: KOWALCZYK

units.text: He looks at the watch for a long moment, then pushes it a few inches back toward her.
